analysis.title: Is client spend on AI starting to disappoint? From free-for-all to token rationing
key_insights: Tech stocks retreated this past week and fixed income yields fell as investors sought safe haven in government securities. Many tech stocks trade at elevated multiples and so act as long-duration assets.

Equity investors have focused on earnings growth momentum and have been resilient despite higher longer-dated Treasury yields. The recent stumble at OpenAI suggests the upward trajectory may be levelling off. If confirmed over coming weeks, it could herald a larger stock reversal, which adds to the attractiveness of core rates markets.

A private portfolio company reported that its underlying firms were flattening AI spend after exponential growth earlier this year. Many non-AI sectors are showing signs of being squeezed by higher rates.

More CEOs are focusing on cost containment, and many managers are rationing token spend after an initial free-for-all. The note does not say AI growth or infrastructure build will slow or stop, only that quarter-on-quarter acceleration across all metrics may moderate. This implies a more modest but still healthy US growth outlook into 2027.

Treasury yields shrugged off somewhat higher US inflation data this week as investors pushed back on speculation of back-to-back Fed hikes later in the month. After meetings with DC policymakers, RBC BlueBay believes the next US hike will not come before December, as the Fed sees little to panic about in recent inflation data.

RBC BlueBay sees US inflation peaking at 4% early in the new year and expects Fed hikes in Q4 and Q1 2027. Base effects should then lower CPI and keep the Fed on hold. Markets are seen as pricing too many Fed hikes for the year ahead, so the firm is constructive on the front of the yield curve.

The firm is more cautious on longer-dated bonds. Growing government and corporate debt could lead markets to demand higher term premia, and with curves relatively flat on both sides of the Atlantic it is biased toward steepening.

Energy prices are a wildcard. Nothing heard from the US administration suggests a plan to end the Middle East conflict. The baseline is oil at current levels, the chance of a sustainable de-escalation deal is low, and regional escalation could push prices much higher.
The Fed would welcome a pullback in tech stocks and self-moderation in AI enthusiasm. Using policy to cool AI-related demand risks doing a lot of damage to the rest of the US economy.

Europe largely followed US moves, with some recovery in sovereign spreads. In the UK, Conservative Party poll gains may limit PM Burnham's ability to call an early election next year, risking a policy agenda of little substance. A UK budget is upcoming.

Japanese government bonds performed well, helped by news of increased buying from domestic investors. The reversal in US stocks has slowed the dollar's recent upward momentum. The firm has no strong view on major FX crosses but highlights the Hungarian forint on building hopes for medium-term euro membership.

Little data is scheduled for the second half of the month and focus shifts to central banks. RBC BlueBay doubts any major central bank will hike at its next meeting, which could give rates a more stable backdrop.

sector_views.rationale: Tech stocks retreated on signs of flattening AI spend. Elevated multiples make them long-duration assets, and a reversal is possible if the earnings growth trajectory levels off.

macro_indicators.interpretation: RBC BlueBay expects US inflation to peak at 4% early in the new year, then decline on base effects, keeping the Fed on hold after Q1 2027.
The report says CPI in the mid-3s is still far below the 2022 peak above 8%, but the trajectory of inflation will determine the rate path.
Cited as a historical comparison for current inflation.

macro_indicators.reading: Hikes in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027; next hike not before December
macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed is expected to hike twice more, then hold. Markets are seen as pricing too many hikes, supporting a constructive view on front-end yields.
Policymakers are motivated to move inflation toward the target over the coming year given the long overshoot and the risk to inflation expectations.
Baseline is oil at current levels, with upside risk to energy prices if the Middle East conflict escalates.

trade_ideas.description: Constructive on the front end of the yield curve (government bonds)
trade_ideas.rationale: Markets have priced too many Fed hikes for the year ahead, and the Fed is expected to hold after Q1 2027.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher-than-expected inflation or energy price escalation could force more hikes.

trade_ideas.description: Curve steepening bias, cautious on longer-dated bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: Rising government and corporate debt could lead markets to demand higher term premia, and curves are relatively flat on both sides of the Atlantic.

trade_ideas.description: Core rates markets favoured over equities if the AI spending slowdown is confirmed
trade_ideas.rationale: A possible stock reversal adds to the attractiveness of core rates.

risk_factors: Energy price escalation from the Middle East conflict.
A flattening of AI spend could trigger a significant stock reversal.
Rising government and corporate debt raising term premia.
Inflation staying above target and affecting forward price expectations.
The UK budget and a possible weak policy agenda from PM Burnham.
vol_and_positioning: Tech stocks trade at extremely elevated multiples and behave like long-duration assets, yet the recent rise in longer-dated Treasury yields did not dent equity bull enthusiasm much.
Equity investors are focused on earnings growth momentum. Any levelling off could trigger a more significant reversal in stocks.
geopolitical: Ongoing conflict in the Middle East with no apparent US administration plan to end it. A sustainable de-escalation deal is seen as unlikely and regional escalation could push energy prices much higher.
UK politics: Conservative Party poll gains may limit PM Burnham's ability to call an early election next year.

tension_points.bull_case: AI growth and infrastructure build are not set to slow or stop, and equity investors have been resilient with a focus on earnings growth momentum.
tension_points.bear_case: Token spend is being rationed, a portfolio company reports flattening AI spend, and the OpenAI stumble suggests quarter-on-quarter acceleration is moderating, which could herald a larger stock reversal.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A continued pattern of quarter-on-quarter acceleration across AI metrics would undermine the bear case. Confirmation of the levelling off over the coming weeks would support it.

tension_points.bull_case: The next hike comes no earlier than December, the Fed sees little to panic about, and CPI declines on base effects after Q1 2027, so markets are pricing too many hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation peaks at 4% early in the new year, energy prices are a wildcard, and the Fed may need to react to them.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Escalation of the Middle East conflict pushing energy prices much higher.

theme_stances.key_argument: Quarter-on-quarter acceleration in AI spending across all metrics may be starting to moderate, though growth and build-out continue.
theme_stances.evidence: token spend is starting to be rationed by many managers

theme_stances.key_argument: Markets have priced too many Fed hikes, so the front of the curve is attractive, while rising debt supply favours steepening.
theme_stances.evidence: markets have priced too many Fed hikes for the year ahead
